title: FROGDNA
standfirst: The largest FakeRare painting, at 1.65m tall. Eighty-eight pixels sampled from eighty-eight Pepes, then hand-painted.

blocks.text: DNA of a pixelated frog
FROGDNA is the largest FakeRare painting at 1.65m tall.
Sampling
Pepe was sampled from 88 Pepe cards in Series 0, Series 1 and Series 2.
Samples were sequenced into 88 pixels via a 'greedy' AI algorithm.
Each pixel was color matched then hand-painted.
The translation
The FROGDNA project re-grounds the pixel back into the material world by translating digital hex codes into the richness of physical paint.

Each color began as a precise digital value, interpreted into painterly recipes... shifting the language of screens into the textures of brush and pigment. Our digital addiction plainly seen inhabiting a physical reality.
1966 ... Gerhard Richter
The project is in conversation with Gerhard Richter's Color Charts (1966), which array industrial colors into grids that question perception, chance, and order.

blocks.caption: Gerhard Richter, colour charts, installation view. Not a MintFace work.

blocks.text: While Richter reorders an industrial reality, MintFace reorders our digital preoccupation.
2022 ... the lineage
The lineage for FROGDNA began with the **[10k Project](/10k)**, minted May 7th 2022. A pixel-centric commentary on the dominance of profile pictures as identity.

**[Seize and Share](/c/seize-and-share)** followed in June 2022, beginning with a reinterpretation of 6529 Seizing Meme #1. The smallest unit of the digital image, the pixel, as a networked art object.
2025 ... exhibition
FROGDNA is being exhibited at The Line in New Zealand.
The 1/1 physical painting has been collected by New Zealand art patrons Mr A & S Novak in July 2025.
Availability
The 1/1 physical painting has been collected. The digital work is minted in the FakeRare collection as 88 editions, on Bitcoin as a Counterparty asset, with 30 of them wrapped for Ethereum.
